_comment_purpose: Vocab overlay for --mode report (finance variant). Merged on top of templates/agents/finance/vocab.json by setup.sh; only fields whose meaning changes under report mode appear here. Fields not listed inherit from the base finance vocab.
_comment_scope: Report mode redeploys only the referee* trio plus the audit agents — none of the generative agents (idea-generator, theory-generator, scorer, self-attacker, paper-writer) run. Their vocab keys (IDEA_*, THEORY_*, SCORER_*, SELF_ATTACK_*, etc.) are therefore irrelevant; we override only what the referee* bodies (which DO run, with shared_modes/report/ body overlays) actually need rewritten.
_comment_referee_journal_role: The base referee-core.md treats the paper as if produced by this pipeline (its own draft). Under report mode the paper is an external submission under review; we re-anchor the journal-role string so the referee internalizes that framing in the report header and in any prose that quotes the role.
REFEREE_JOURNAL_ROLE: **top-3 finance journal** (JF, JFE, RFS), evaluating an external submission under review
_comment_inherited_bullets: REFEREE_MIDDLE_BULLETS and REFEREE_FINAL_BULLET are intentionally NOT overridden. The base finance values ('Does the paper answer the question correctly? / Are the results robust...' / 'Does it pass the so what test?') are appropriate for external-submission refereeing and reused as-is. If a future editor finds these unreferenced in a report-only deployment, that is by design — the report-mode overlay of referee-core.md still expands them.
_comment_mech_eval_frame: The report-mode referee-mechanism overlay body keys its evaluative frame; report mode names the math-auditor explicitly (the base value says 'another referee'), so the frame is re-anchored here per variant.
MECH_EVAL_FRAME: **You evaluate whether the paper's economic mechanism works as economics** — not whether the math is correct (the math-auditor handles that), not whether the paper fits the journal (the editorial referee handles that). Your question is: does the economic force the paper invokes actually deliver the result the paper claims, through the channel the paper claims, for reasons a seminar audience would find convincing?
